topic: Your brain's best guess 4: People are happier to help than you think
caption:
People are happier to help than you think.

The prediction: asking for help is a burden on the other person.

In studies, people asking for help underestimated how willing others were, and how good helping felt for them. We tend to see helping as obligation, and overlook how often people genuinely want to help.

Something to try: consider asking for one small piece of help this week.

Your brain's best guess is our series on everyday predictions that research suggests are often too pessimistic. Studies were with US participants and mostly small requests, so results may differ for you.

Research: Zhao, X., & Epley, N. (2022). Surprisingly happy to have helped: Underestimating prosociality creates a misplaced barrier to asking for help. Psychological Science, 33(10), 1708-1731. https://doi.org/10.1177/09567976221097615
